status: Research suggestions, not reservations. Check live claims and open PRs.

tracks.useful_outcome: Frontier results re-timed on hardware other than the original Apple M2, or a harness that makes that possible.

tasks.question: Does the C3 reconstruction-fusion squaring gain (about 3% wall time at 4,096-16,384 limbs on M2) reproduce on another Apple Silicon chip (M1, M3, M4, Pro/Max variants)?
methods: Follow the Reproduce commands in docs/experiments-m2.md with -mcpu set for your chip; run the A/A control first, then both confirmation seeds.
Same, but with the M2 flags unchanged (-mcpu=apple-m2), to separate tuning from microarchitecture.
tasks.acceptance_gate: Control interval includes zero; both confirmation runs reported with CPU and wall aggregates and 95% intervals; chip, macOS, clang version and CFLAGS stated; raw results directory committed under results/. A null or negative result is equally acceptable.

first_step.scope: Positive control: the patch file is present and well-formed. Building needs Apple Silicon macOS and the README prerequisites.

tasks.first_experiment: make && sh scripts/build_harness.sh, build repro-control and repro-c3, then the repro-control comparison; stop and report if the control interval excludes zero.
tasks.bottleneck_link: All frontier evidence is from one M2; a second chip is the cheapest way to test whether the gain is algorithmic.
allowed_variations: Other operand sizes in addition to (not instead of) the documented confirmation sizes
scope_change_triggers: The harness needs code changes to run on your chip: switch to harness-linux-port's scope and say so

tasks.question: Do the prepared-input polynomial-matrix gains (4.34-15.09% CPU) or the theta batch gains (3.65/4.92/5.84%) reproduce on a non-M2 machine?
methods: Polynomial matrices: build poly-prepared and poly-contiguous-control, validate, then compare_poly.py with the confirm plan.
Theta: rebuild the theta-batch retained candidate and rerun its confirmation slice.
tasks.acceptance_gate: Validation passes; per-case CPU intervals for every case in the plan, with machine details and an A/A or control comparison; raw results committed.

first_step.scope: Positive control: the patch is present and well-formed.

tasks.bottleneck_link: Second-architecture evidence for the strongest eligible paths is item 3 of the project plan's follow-through.
scope_change_triggers: Only part of the plan can run on your machine: report the subset explicitly

tasks.question: Can the build and timing harness run on Linux (x86-64 and aarch64) without changing what it measures?
methods: Parameterize prefixes, CFLAGS and shared-library names; load two FLINT builds side by side with dlopen(RTLD_LOCAL) on Linux.
Run in a container first, then on bare metal for timing.
tasks.acceptance_gate: make check passes on Linux; an A/A comparison of two identical builds gives intervals including zero; macOS behaviour unchanged (re-run make check there or state that you couldn't).
tasks.bottleneck_link: Most donor hardware is not Apple Silicon; without a Linux harness, replication can't use it.

tracks.useful_outcome: Independent rechecks of the frontier, and repairs to evidence that a stranger can't currently check.

tasks.question: Do the frontier's headline numbers follow from the committed raw samples under the documented estimators, when re-derived independently?
methods: Replay: run scripts/check_frontier.py and audit what it actually checks.
Reimplement: write your own estimator from the method descriptions in the docs, without reading check_frontier.py, and compare.
tasks.acceptance_gate: A verification record at research/frontier-recheck/verifications/<date>-<handle>.json with method, outcome, scope and not_checked; any discrepancy quoted with file and number.

first_step.scope: Re-derives statistics from committed samples; re-times nothing.

tasks.bottleneck_link: One independent recheck plus maintainer review is the acceptance rule; this is the cheapest such check.

tasks.question: docs/review-report.md and docs/review-reproduction.md cite patches/0001-0005-*.patch, reproduce/, evidence/, REPRODUCE.md, PROCESS-AUDITS.md and SHA256SUMS, none of which exist here. Which patches/opt-*.patch files (including -v2 variants) are the five reviewed patches, and can the references be made to resolve?
starting_points: docs/flint-optimization-campaign.md (line ~139 still says the objective is incomplete)
methods: Map each cited patch to an opt-*.patch file by content and hashes recorded under results/flint-optimization-campaign/, then fix the references.
Regenerate the missing package with scripts/package_optimization_campaign.py if its inputs are committed.
tasks.acceptance_gate: Every path cited in both review docs resolves, or is marked as not retained; the mapping is justified by hashes; the stale status line is corrected with a pointer to review-report.md.

first_step.scope: Confirms the reference gap: the listing contains opt-*.patch files but no 0001-*.patch files.

tasks.bottleneck_link: Reviewers and upstream maintainers can't check the review series until its references resolve.

tasks.question: Can the retained-result audits (audit_experiments, audit_poly_prepared, audit_theta_batch, audit_theta_equal) be split so that the data checks run from a fresh clone, leaving build-fingerprint checks optional?
methods: Add a --data-only mode that skips local-artifact hashes and sister imports, keeping every check on committed files.
Vendor the small sister-repo functions that the audits need, with their source commit recorded.
tasks.acceptance_gate: In a fresh clone without .deps/ or ../integerMult, each audit's data-only mode passes; on the original machine, the full mode still passes unchanged.

first_step.scope: Shows the sibling-repo dependency pattern. In a fresh clone, python3 scripts/audit_theta_batch.py fails with ModuleNotFoundError: No module named 'exclusion_circuit'.

tasks.bottleneck_link: Verification by other contributors only works if they can run the checks.

tracks.useful_outcome: Patches a FLINT maintainer could review: portable, fully tested, memory-profiled, with dispatch and accuracy scope stated.

tasks.question: The C3 patch is described as M2-specific, but it uses only FLINT's vec8d/vec4n abstractions, with no NEON intrinsics. Does it build, pass the fft_small tests, and keep a gain on x86-64 with FLINT's AVX2 backend?
starting_points: FLINT src/machine_vectors.h at the commit in deps.json
methods: Apply to the pinned FLINT on x86-64 Linux, configure with AVX2, run make check MOD=fft_small; then time if harness-linux-port has landed.
Audit the vector operations it uses against each backend in machine_vectors.h and list any that lack an AVX2 implementation.
tasks.acceptance_gate: Build and fft_small test log on x86-64; a corrected portability statement for docs/experiments-m2.md; timing with an A/A control if measured.

first_step.scope: Lists the FLINT vector operations the patch uses. grep -cE 'vld1|vst1|vreinterpret|arm_neon|__aarch64__' on the same file prints 0: no direct NEON intrinsics. That doesn't prove the backends are equivalent.

tasks.bottleneck_link: Portability is a precondition for proposing C3 upstream (docs/experiments-m2.md).

tasks.question: Is the combined theta patch (direct-walsh + batch-retained, optionally equal-bank) ready for maintainer review: correctness scope, dispatch conditions, accuracy checks and timing controls stated?
methods: Run FLINT's acb_theta tests on the patched tree and add tests for the new paths.
Write the dispatch conditions and accuracy argument as a reviewer-facing note.
tasks.acceptance_gate: acb_theta tests pass on the patched tree (log committed); a review note covering correctness, dispatch, accuracy and timing evidence, with prior-art attribution as in docs/project-plan.md.

first_step.scope: Lists the files the theta patches touch.

tasks.bottleneck_link: Preparing the theta patch for maintainer review is follow-through item 2 of the project plan.

tasks.question: Do the five review-series patches pass FLINT's full test suite, and what do they cost in memory?
methods: Full make check on FLINT 26b9bc9d with the series applied.
Peak RSS and allocation counts for each patch's benchmark cases, before and after.
tasks.acceptance_gate: Full-suite log with the base commit and the patch hashes; a memory table per patch with method stated.

first_step.scope: Positive control: the patch file is present and well-formed.

tasks.bottleneck_link: No full-library test run and no memory profile are listed obligations before upstream submission.

tracks.useful_outcome: A genuine complete caller, or the missing inputs for one, profiled before any new timing campaign.

tasks.question: Is there real software, such as a published computation or a library built on FLINT, whose complete run spends a material share of time in nmod_poly_mat multiplication, acb_theta evaluation or large-integer squaring at the frontier's sizes?
methods: Search published code (Sage, Oscar, Magma ports, number-theory papers with code) for call sites, then profile one complete run.
Instrument FLINT to count calls and sizes in one candidate's run.
tasks.acceptance_gate: A named caller with reproducible inputs and a profile showing the share of time in the patched routine at the relevant sizes; an opportunity estimate (share × measured gain) before any timing. A documented null result is acceptable.

first_step.scope: Names the entry point a caller would have to reach.

tasks.bottleneck_link: No genuine downstream caller exists for any frontier result; synthetic fixtures limit what the gains mean.

tasks.question: Can the genus-six period matrix for Elkies-Kieffer (arXiv:2505.22382, Section 6.3) be produced to 120 digits with provenance, unblocking the E4 benchmark?
methods: Run scripts/export_theta_e4.m in Magma and commit the tagged export with the log.
Compute the period matrix with open tools (e.g. Sage's RiemannSurface) and cross-check the symmetry assertion and the E4 value against the paper.
tasks.acceptance_gate: A committed export in THETA_E4_V1 format, plus the tool, version and log; an independent cross-check of at least one invariant against the paper.

first_step.expected: // Elkies--Kieffer arXiv:2505.22382, Section 6.3: base curve only.
first_step.scope: Locates the export script and its stated limits.

tasks.bottleneck_link: Genus-six E4 is the next theta target and is blocked only on this input.
